contamination.label: Covariate contamination (lambda)
contamination.help: How much of the post-5-March move in the ruble, equities and CPI you attribute to the sanctions package rather than to the war. At 0 the controls are treated as pure war signal and the counterfactual is allowed to use them raw. At 1 they are restored to their pre-announcement level, on the view that letting a sanctions-driven ruble into the control set launders payment effects into the counterfactual and shrinks the estimated payment damage.

war_exposure.label: Russia/Ukraine war exposure (phi)
war_exposure.help: For every 1% the war took off Ukrainian e-commerce, how much it took off Russian. 1.0 means proportional in logs. Calibrated by default on 24 February to 4 March, the only window with war and intact rails.

anticipation_days.label: Anticipation buffer (trading days)
anticipation_days.help: Trading days before the announcement dropped from the estimation sample. Russian consumers and banks had warning; pre-positioning left in the training data is learned as normal behaviour and biases the counterfactual toward the already-depressed path.

intervention_date.label: Intervention date
intervention_date.help: Announcement (5 March) versus first observable degradation in card acceptance (7 March). Announcement effects and operational effects are different treatments.

key_window.label: Two-week assessment window
key_window.help: Which ten trading days the headline number covers.

baseline_covariate_rule.label: No-shock covariate path
baseline_covariate_rule.help: How macro controls are assumed to have evolved in a world with no war at all: frozen at their pre-war level, or continuing their pre-war trend.

controls.label: Control set
controls.help: Which series the counterfactual is allowed to condition on. Card-availability series are never selectable: they are the treatment.

arima_order.label: ARIMA order (p,d,q)
arima_order.help: Dynamic specification. (1,0,3) was selected on AIC/BIC over the pre-intervention sample.

bsts_time_varying.label: Allow control loadings to drift
bsts_time_varying.help: Lets the mapping from macro conditions to e-commerce change through the war. Switching it off imposes that the pre-war relationship held unchanged across the invasion.

bsts_seasonality.label: Day-of-week component
bsts_seasonality.help: Trading-week cycle in the state vector.

bsts_level_scale.label: Local level prior scale
bsts_level_scale.help: How freely the underlying level is allowed to wander. Larger values let the counterfactual track recent drift and widen the bands.

rf_lags.label: Autoregressive lags in the forest
rf_lags.help: Adding lagged outcomes gives the forest dynamics it otherwise lacks and removes most of the serial correlation in its residuals.

rf_max_depth.label: Forest depth
rf_max_depth.help: Capacity. Deeper trees fit the pre-period harder and extrapolate no better.

gru_members.label: Ensemble members
gru_members.help: Independent networks averaged. Ensemble spread is most of the reported uncertainty.

dose_lags.label: Dose response lags
dose_lags.help: Trading days over which a change in card availability is allowed to pass through to volume.

did_pre_days.label: Pre-period length (trading days)
did_pre_days.help: Window used to fit the Russian and Ukrainian trends. Longer windows are more stable and less local to the pre-war level.

carima.label: Controls unaffected by the treatment
carima.statement: The covariates used to project the counterfactual would have taken the same path had the card networks stayed up.
carima.why: A control that the treatment moved is a post-treatment variable. Conditioning on it absorbs part of the payment effect into the counterfactual and biases the estimate toward zero.
carima.evidence: The ruble, the RTS oil and gas index and CPI all move violently after 5 March, and the card suspension was part of the same sanctions wave that moved them. The contamination slider is the direct stress test.

carima.label: Conditional stationarity
carima.statement: Given the controls, the outcome process is stable across the intervention date.
carima.why: The counterfactual is the pre-period process run forward. If the process itself broke at the invasion, that projection is not the counterfactual.
carima.evidence: The invasion is eleven trading days before the announcement. Volatility, level and the covariance with macro controls all shift. This is the weakest assumption in the whole exercise and the reason for the three-path decomposition rather than a single pre/post comparison.

carima.label: Constant residual variance
carima.statement: Innovation variance does not change across the sample.
carima.why: Interval coverage, not the point estimate, depends on this. Understated variance turns an insignificant effect into a significant one.
carima.evidence: Breusch-Pagan rejects decisively for the parametric models. Intervals here are built from a residual bootstrap rather than the analytic formula for that reason.

carima.label: No anticipation
carima.statement: Behaviour before the announcement is unaffected by the coming suspension.
carima.why: Anticipatory stockpiling or card-switching before 5 March is learned by the model as normal pre-period behaviour, which drags the counterfactual down and understates the damage.
carima.evidence: Sanctions were widely trailed and the sample shows an unusual 3-4 March spike in volume consistent with pull-forward. The anticipation buffer removes those days from estimation.

carima.label: Linear, invertible ARMA dynamics
carima.statement: The outcome follows a stable linear recursion in its own lags and the controls.
carima.why: The forecast is generated by iterating that recursion; a misspecified lag structure compounds with horizon.
carima.evidence: Ljung-Box on in-sample residuals is reported in the diagnostics panel. The AR block is constrained to the stationary region so the counterfactual cannot diverge.

carima.label: Single, persistent, well-defined treatment
carima.statement: The suspension is one intervention, it does not reverse inside the window, and every unit of the outcome is exposed to the same treatment.
carima.why: Without it there is no single counterfactual to recover; the estimand itself is undefined.
carima.evidence: Visa, MasterCard and peers suspended over 5-10 March 2022 and did not restore service inside the sample. The card-availability series go to zero and stay there through 30 December 2022.

bsts.label: Correct state decomposition
bsts.statement: Level, weekly cycle and control regression exhaust the systematic variation, with Gaussian errors.
bsts.why: An omitted state component is absorbed into the level, which then drifts to fit it and carries that drift into the counterfactual.
bsts.evidence: Residual diagnostics pass here where the other models fail, which is the main evidence for this specification. Over-specification is the standing risk: a very flexible level can track the post-shock path and report no effect.

rf.evidence: The ruble, the RTS oil and gas index and CPI all move violently after 5 March, and the card suspension was part of the same sanctions wave that moved them. The contamination slider is the direct stress test.

rf.label: Counterfactual lies inside observed support
rf.statement: The no-suspension path stays within the range of outcomes the model saw in training.
rf.why: Tree ensembles predict averages of training leaves. They cannot return a value outside the training range, whatever the covariates say.
rf.evidence: Early March volume ran above anything in 2021, so the forest's counterfactual is censored at the pre-period maximum and the payment effect it reports is a lower bound in magnitude.

rf.label: No anticipation

rf.evidence: Sanctions were widely trailed and the sample shows an unusual 3-4 March spike in volume consistent with pull-forward. The anticipation buffer removes those days from estimation.

rf.label: Independent residuals
rf.why: Bootstrap intervals built on resampled residuals are only valid if the residuals are exchangeable; dependence makes them far too narrow.
rf.evidence: The static forest fails Ljung-Box at every lag tested. Adding autoregressive lags is the repair, and the diagnostics panel shows whether it worked.

gru.label: No structural identification
gru.statement: The model provides predictive accuracy, not a causal argument.
gru.why: Stated plainly so the number is not read as an estimate with the same standing as the design-based ones.
gru.evidence: Included to bound how much of the gap is explained by nonlinearity in the outcome-control mapping rather than by the intervention.

gru.evidence: Sanctions were widely trailed and the sample shows an unusual 3-4 March spike in volume consistent with pull-forward. The anticipation buffer removes those days from estimation.

gru.label: Capacity matched to sample
gru.statement: The network is small enough not to memorise roughly 420 pre-intervention days.
gru.why: An overfitted sequence model reproduces the training path and its counterfactual is noise with a confident band around it.
gru.evidence: Held down with weight decay, dropout and a 32-unit hidden state, and averaged over an ensemble. There is no identification argument here; the model is a flexibility benchmark, not a causal estimator on its own.

gru.evidence: Visa, MasterCard and peers suspended over 5-10 March 2022 and did not restore service inside the sample. The card-availability series go to zero and stay there through 30 December 2022.

did.label: Parallel trends, adjusted for exposure
did.statement: Absent the suspension, Russian and Ukrainian e-commerce would have moved together up to the exposure elasticity phi.
did.why: This is what licenses reading the war channel off Ukraine instead of assuming it.
did.evidence: Pre-war trends can be compared directly in the dashboard. The two economies differ in size, penetration and war role, which is exactly what phi is for, and why phi is exposed as a slider rather than fixed.

did.label: Control is untreated
did.statement: Ukrainian e-commerce was not itself hit by the Visa/MasterCard suspension in Russia.
did.why: A contaminated control absorbs the treatment effect and collapses the estimate toward zero.
did.evidence: The suspension applied to cards issued in or used in Russia. Ukrainian card rails stayed live; Visa and MasterCard continued operating in Ukraine throughout.

dose.label: Controls unaffected by the treatment
dose.statement: The covariates used to project the counterfactual would have taken the same path had the card networks stayed up.
dose.why: A control that the treatment moved is a post-treatment variable. Conditioning on it absorbs part of the payment effect into the counterfactual and biases the estimate toward zero.
dose.evidence: The ruble, the RTS oil and gas index and CPI all move violently after 5 March, and the card suspension was part of the same sanctions wave that moved them. The contamination slider is the direct stress test.

dose.label: Rollout timing unrelated to war news
dose.statement: The four-day staircase in card availability is not systematically timed with the war shocks hitting demand on the same days.
dose.why: The dose coefficients would otherwise pick up whatever else moved on 7-10 March.
dose.evidence: The rollout schedule was set by network operations, not by the front line, which supports the claim. But the same fortnight carried the central bank rate hike and capital controls, which did not.

dose.label: Effect proportional to availability
dose.statement: Losing half of cross-border card acceptance does half the damage of losing all of it.
dose.why: The counterfactual is built by accumulating the dose response, so curvature in the response maps straight into bias.
dose.evidence: Plausible over a four-day window, weak over months as substitution to Mir and domestic rails sets in. The estimate is reported for the two-week window only.

models.name: Ukraine difference-in-differences
models.tagline: Uses a war-exposed, payments-unexposed control instead of assuming the war away.

models.name: Dose-response (rollout intensity)
models.tagline: Reads the effect off the four-day staged collapse in card acceptance.

models.name: Bayesian structural time series
models.tagline: Drifting level, weekly cycle, drifting control loadings. Best in-sample fit, widest bands.

models.name: C-ARIMA
models.tagline: Linear dynamics plus controls. Transparent, and the weakest link is stationarity.

models.name: Random forest
models.tagline: Flexible mapping from controls. Cannot extrapolate past observed levels.

models.name: GRU ensemble
models.tagline: Nonlinear dynamics, no interpretable identification. Ensemble bands.
